questions.question: Why must permission enforcement happen at retrieval rather than at the UI?
options: The generator will synthesize and thereby leak whatever enters its context
The UI cannot hide citations reliably
Retrieval is faster than page rendering
Users can disable UI-level filters

questions.question: What does every chunk carry at ingest for ACL-aware retrieval?
options: A tenant-specific encryption key
The document owner's job title
An ACL payload of allowed users, groups, or roles
A signed copy of the source document

questions.question: Ninety percent of the corpus is forbidden to a user. What happens when the pipeline post-filters an ANN top-100?
options: The user gets about 90 eligible candidates
The user keeps about 10 eligible candidates and gets thin answers
The index rebalances itself automatically
The reranker compensates with more depth

questions.question: Why is post-filter starvation also a security issue, not just a quality issue?
options: It slows down legitimate queries
It increases the embedding compute bill
It forces nightly re-indexing
Result-count changes let a prober infer that hidden documents exist

questions.question: Why resolve group membership at query time rather than denormalizing it into documents?
options: Query-time resolution is faster
Membership changes then do not force re-indexing
Documents stay smaller on disk
Group names cannot be indexed anyway

questions.question: A document's ACL is tightened at 14:00. What must happen beyond the metadata update?
options: The document must be re-embedded immediately
The whole index must be rebuilt
Cached retrievals and answers derived from it must be invalidated
All active users must re-authenticate

questions.question: Which isolation option is the weakest?
options: Separate clusters per tenant
Separate indexes per tenant in one cluster
Tenant namespaces within one index
A shared index with tenant_id as an ordinary filter

questions.question: An answer cache is keyed by query text alone. What can happen?
options: Tenant A receives the answer cached for tenant B
Cache entries expire immediately
Queries bypass the retriever entirely
Embedding vectors collide across tenants

questions.question: What does the response layer add when the retrieval filter is already mandatory?
options: Faster page rendering
A second embedding quality check
Re-verification of tenant tags that catches the day the filter has a bug
Load balancing across tenant traffic

questions.question: Where should tenant context come from on every request?
options: A client-supplied query parameter
The authenticated session, injected by the gateway
The document being retrieved
A tenant-selected browser cookie

questions.question: A shared query rewriter is fine-tuned on all tenants' query logs. What is the risk?
options: The model slows down for every tenant
The logs overflow the context window
The rewriter forgets the earliest tenants
One tenant's phrasing can be regurgitated into another tenant's session

questions.question: Why is tenant_id made a first-class schema field from day one?
options: Retrofitting tenant identity into a shared index is a full rebuild with an incident attached
First-class fields compress more efficiently
Filters require alphabetically ordered fields
Namespaces cannot be created after launch

questions.question: What is indirect prompt injection?
options: An attacker queries the model repeatedly to extract its prompt
An attacker fine-tunes the embedding model
Adversarial instructions planted in retrievable content that the pipeline fetches into the context
An attacker edits the system prompt through the admin console

questions.question: Why does retrieval make prompt injection precise?
options: Retrieval encrypts the injected payload
The pipeline delivers the payload exactly when it is most relevant to the question
The reranker amplifies injected text
Retrieved text bypasses the tokenizer

questions.question: Which output pattern suggests an exfiltration attempt via injection?
options: Answers formatted with bullet lists
Answers written in very short sentences
Answers citing multiple sources
Rendered links whose URLs carry conversation data in query parameters

questions.question: What is the structural defense against a compromised reader model?
options: The reader holds no tools or credentials, and an orchestrator consumes only its structured outputs
The reader is retrained on a weekly schedule
The reader uses a smaller context window
The orchestrator rewrites all user queries

questions.question: What is the correct security posture toward prompt injection as of early 2026?
options: Ingest sanitization fully prevents it
Provenance tags eliminate the risk
Assume some injection succeeds and limit what success can reach
Allow only curated documents into the index

questions.question: What does a per-tenant canary document detect?
options: Slow background indexing jobs
Canary strings surfacing in another tenant's answers
Embedding model version drift
Judge model self-preference bias
